mainTopic: The משמרות and מעמדות: rebuilding the watches, why they read מעשה בראשית, their fasts, and how the Sunday reading is divided between readers
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the כהנים who returned from Babylon. Only four of the 24 משמרות came back, so the נביאים divided them into 24 by lottery and ruled that ידעיה keeps first place even if יהויריב returns. The גמרא then asks why the מעמדות read מעשה בראשית. רב אסי answers that the world stands because of the מעמדות. He shows this through אברהם's conversation with הקב״ה about the קרבנות, and he adds that reading the סדר קרבנות counts as bringing them. A ברייתא describes the מעמד fasting Monday through Thursday, each day for a different group in need, but not on Friday or שבת out of כבוד שבת. Three אמוראים give reasons for not fasting on Sunday. Finally, the גמרא asks how two people can read the five פסוקים of בראשית. רב says the second reader repeats a פסוק, and שמואל says they split one. A ברייתא then challenges both of them, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Four returning watches are split into twenty-four by lottery
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the נביאים took the four families of כהנים who returned and divided them into 24 משמרות using a lottery box.
steps.simpleTranslation: They divided them and set them up as twenty-four. They mixed the lots and put them into a box. ידעיה came and drew his own lot and the lots of his companions, six in all. חרים came and drew his own lot and his companions' lots, six in all. The same happened for פשחור and for אמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the full system of 24 priestly watches was rebuilt when only four families came back from Babylon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the four returning families (ידעיה, חרים, פשחור, אמר) drew six lots: one for itself and five for new watches made up from its own members. Four times six gives back the full 24 משמרות.

keyTerms.meaning: A box or urn that lots are drawn from
A priestly watch, a group of כהנים that serves in the מקדש for one week at a time
His own share and the share of his companions

phrases.english: and they divided them and set them up as twenty-four,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the four families of כהנים who came back from Babylon.

phrases.english: they mixed them up and put them into a lottery box.
Jedaiah came and drew
his own portion and his companions' portions, six in all,
Harim came and drew
his own portion and his companions' portions, six in all,
and the same for Pashhur, and the same for Immer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section about the four משמרות that returned from exile.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four returning families were divided by lot into 24 משמרות, six from each family.

steps.title: The prophets rule that Jedaiah keeps first place
steps.stepSummary: The נביאים set a condition: even if יהויריב, the original first watch, returns, ידעיה stays first and יהויריב comes second to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prophets among them also made a condition: even if יהויריב, the head of the watches, comes up, ידעיה will not be pushed out of its place. Rather, ידעיה stays the main one, and יהויריב is secondary to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a ruling about order: the new arrangement stays in place even if the original leading watch later returns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally יהויריב was the first of the 24 watches, but it did not come back from Babylon. The נביאים made sure that if it ever returned, it would not take back first place from ידעיה. It would only be attached to ידעיה as a secondary group.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a condition or stipulation
Will not be pushed aside or demoted
Secondary, attached to the main one

steps.whatToRemember: After the exile, four families were divided into 24 משמרות by lot, and ידעיה permanently took first place, even over יהויריב.

phrases.english: And the prophets among them also stipulated:
that even if Jehoiarib, the head of the watches, comes up,
phrases.notes: "Comes up" here means comes up from exile to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Jedaiah will not be pushed out of its place.
Rather, Jedaiah is the main one,
and Jehoiarib is secondary to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about the order of the newly formed משמרות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ידעיה stays first among the משמרות even if יהויריב returns; יהויריב would be secondary to it.

steps.title: The משנה: Israelites of the watch read the Creation story
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the ordinary Israelites linked to the serving משמר gather in their towns and read מעשה בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Israelites of that watch gather in their towns and read the account of Creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a new line so that it can ask about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each priestly משמר had a matching group of ordinary Jews (the מעמד). When their week came, those who stayed home gathered in their own towns and read the Creation section of the Torah. The גמרא is setting up a question about why this particular section is read.

keyTerms.meaning: A group of ordinary Jews paired with a priestly משמר
The account of Creation at the start of בראשית

phrases.english: And the Israelites of that watch
gather in their towns
and read the account of Creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ברייתא and opens a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Israelites of the serving משמר gather in their towns and read מעשה בראשית.

steps.title: Where does this practice come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of reading מעשה בראשית at the מעמדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these words derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the source or reason is for reading the Creation story at the מעמדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack. The גמרא wants to know why this section of the Torah was chosen and what connects it to the מעמדות.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (derived)? A standard request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these words derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and reason for reading מעשה בראשית at the מעמדות.

steps.title: Heaven and earth exist because of the watches
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי teaches that without the מעמדות, heaven and earth would not keep existing. He brings a פסוק in which אברהם asks how he will inherit the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אחא said in the name of רב אסי: Were it not for the מעמדות, heaven and earth would not continue to exist, as it says: "And he said, Lord God, by what shall I know that I will inherit it?"
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by linking the מעמדות to the continued existence of the whole world, using a פסוק about אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the choice of reading: the מעמדות, and the service they stand for, keep Creation going, so it fits to read about Creation. The פסוק on its own does not show this yet. The next steps explain how it does.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק does not mention מעמדות or קרבנות at all. Wait for the next steps, where the גמרא explains the hidden meaning.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Aḥa said that Rav Asi said:
Were it not for the non-priestly watches,
heaven and earth would not continue to exist,
as it is said: "And he said: Lord God,
by what shall I know that I will inherit it?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The world exists because of the מעמדות, which is why they read about Creation. This is supported by the פסוק of אברהם's question.

steps.title: Abraham asks whether his children will be destroyed for sinning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the פסוק: אברהם asked whether his children would be destroyed for their sins like the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Tower, and הקב״ה said no.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said: Master of the Universe! Perhaps the Jewish people will sin before You. Will You do to them as You did to the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion? He said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining what אברהם was really asking in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם's worry was not only about owning the land. He feared his descendants might be wiped out for sinning, like earlier generations were. הקב״ה promised that this would not happen, which leads to the next question: what will protect them?

keyTerms.meaning: The generation of the Dispersion (the Tower of Bavel)

phrases.english: Abraham said: Master of the Universe!
Perhaps the Jewish people will sin before You,
will You do to them
as to the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion?
He said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אברהם's question was whether his sinning descendants would be destroyed. הקב״ה answered no.

steps.title: God hints at the sacrifices as the answer
steps.stepSummary: אברהם asks how his descendants will keep the land, and הקב״ה answers with the command to take animals for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: Master of the Universe! Tell me, by what will I inherit it? He said to him: "Take for Me a three-year-old heifer and a three-year-old goat, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם asks what will protect his children, and הקב״ה answers by telling him to bring animals for offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals in הקב״ה's answer hint at the קרבנות. In their merit the Jewish people, and through them the world, are protected. This links back to רב אסי's claim that the world exists because of the מעמדות, which stood alongside the קרבנות in the מקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base of the idea that the קרבנות, and the מעמדות that went with them, keep the world going. That is why the מעמדות read מעשה בראשית.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
Tell me, by what will I inherit it?
He said to him: "Take for Me a three-year-old heifer
and a three-year-old goat, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 15:9. The animals hint at the קרבנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם! הוֹדִיעֵנִי בַּמֶּה אִירָשֶׁנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the dialogue: after the promise not to destroy them, אברהם asks what will protect them.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקב״ה's answer points to the קרבנות as the merit that protects the Jewish people and the world.

steps.title: Abraham asks what happens when there is no Temple
steps.stepSummary: אברהם asks הקב״ה: the קרבנות work while the בית המקדש stands, but what will protect his children when it is destroyed?
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said: Master of the World, this is fine while the בית המקדש stands. But when it no longer stands, what will become of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The story of אברהם and הקב״ה continues. אברהם pushes further and asks what will protect his children once the בית המקדש is gone, and this sets up הקב״ה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, הקב״ה said the קרבנות would keep אברהם's children safe. אברהם now points to a gap in that answer: קרבנות can only be brought while there is a בית המקדש. So he asks what will protect them in exile.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World, a way of speaking directly to הקב״ה
It is fine, it works out (for this case)

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
phrases.notes: "He" is אברהם, still speaking to הקב״ה as in the earlier steps.

phrases.english: This works out well when the Temple is standing.
But when the Temple is not standing,
what will become of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the answer in step 7, since קרבנות need a בית המקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What will protect אברהם's descendants when there is no בית המקדש and no קרבנות?

steps.title: Reading about the offerings counts like bringing them
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה answers that He already set up the סדר קרבנות. When the Jews read it, He counts it as if they brought the קרבנות, and He forgives all their sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I already set up for them the order of the קרבנות. When they read it before Me, I count it as if they offered them before Me, and I forgive them for all their sins.
steps.whatsHappening: הקב״ה answers אברהם: reading the passages about the קרבנות takes the place of actually bringing them. This explains why the קרבנות, and the reading at the מעמדות, keep the world going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם's worry was that without a בית המקדש there is no way to bring קרבנות. The answer is that reading the סדר קרבנות counts as if they were brought and earns forgiveness. This finishes רב אסי's answer: the world stands because of the קרבנות, so the people of the מעמד read מעשה בראשית, the story of the world's creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the offerings, the passages describing the קרבנות
I count it for them as if

steps.whatToRemember: Reading the סדר קרבנות counts as if the קרבנות were brought. Since the קרבנות keep the world existing, the מעמד reads מעשה בראשית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the custom of saying the passages about the קרבנות in our daily תפילה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּבָר תִּקַּנְתִּי לָהֶם סֵדֶר קׇרְבָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: He said to him: I have already set up for them the order of offerings.
When they read them before Me,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֲנִי עֲלֵיהֶם כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרִיבוּם לְפָנַי
phrases.english: I count it for them as though they had offered them before Me,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי מוֹחֵל לָהֶם עַל כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: and I forgive them for all their sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אברהם's question from step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reading the סדר קרבנות counts as if they were offered and brings forgiveness, even without a בית המקדש.

steps.title: What the priestly watch and the non-priestly watch did
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the men of the משמר prayed that their brothers' קרבן be accepted. The men of the מעמד gathered in the synagogue and fasted four days: Monday through Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the men of the משמר would pray that their brothers' offering be accepted with favor. The men of the מעמד would gather in the synagogue and keep four fasts: on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes what each group did during their week of service. The men of the מעמד fasted on four days of the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two groups are described. The משמר, the כהנים serving in the בית המקדש, prayed for the קרבנות. The מעמד, the ordinary Israelites linked to that משמר, gathered in shul back home and fasted from Monday to Thursday. The next steps explain what each fast day was for and why other days were left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Men of the watch: the כהנים serving that week
Men of the station: the ordinary Israelites linked to that משמר

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר הָיוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין
phrases.english: The Sages taught: The members of the priestly watch would pray
for the offering of their brothers, that it should be accepted with favor.
And the members of the non-priestly watch would gather in the synagogue
and keep four fasts:
on Monday of the week, on Tuesday, on Wednesday, and on Thursday.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר הָיוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reason for reading מעשה בראשית to a ברייתא describing what the משמר and מעמד did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משמר prayed for the קרבנות. The מעמד gathered in shul and fasted Monday through Thursday.

steps.title: What each fast day was for
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists each fast day's purpose. Monday was for sea travelers, Tuesday for desert travelers, Wednesday against croup in children, and Thursday for pregnant and nursing women.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Monday they fasted for those traveling by sea. On Tuesday, for those traveling through deserts. On Wednesday, that the disease of croup should not strike the children. On Thursday, for pregnant and nursing women: for pregnant women, that they should not miscarry; for nursing women, that they should be able to nurse their children.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and tells us whom the people of the מעמד prayed for on each of the four fast days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day has its own group of people in danger or in need. These days line up with what was created on each day of מעשה בראשית: sea, dry land, the lights, and living creatures. That fits the fact that the מעמד read מעשה בראשית.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go down to the sea, sea travelers
Croup, a deadly throat disease of children

phrases.english: On Monday, for seafarers.
On Tuesday, for those who travel through deserts.
On Wednesday, about croup,
that it should not strike the children.
On Thursday, for pregnant women and nursing women.
Pregnant women, that they should not miscarry;
nursing women, that they should be able to nurse their children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what each of the four fast days listed in step 10 was for.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each fast day had its own purpose: sea travelers, desert travelers, children's health, and pregnant and nursing women.

steps.title: No fasting on Friday or Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that they did not fast on ערב שבת, out of respect for שבת. By a קל וחומר, they certainly did not fast on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב שבת they did not fast, out of respect for שבת. All the more so, they did not fast on שבת itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the fasting stopped on Thursday: no fasting on Friday because of שבת, and certainly not on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fasting on Friday would mean starting שבת hungry and weak, which is not proper honor for שבת. If even the day before שבת is protected, שבת itself is surely protected; that is the קל וחומר. This still leaves Sunday unexplained, which the גמרא asks about next.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; reasoning from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: And on Shabbat eve they would not fast,
out of respect for Shabbat,
and all the more so on Shabbat itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לֹא הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why Friday and שבת are not among the fast days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No fasting on ערב שבת because of כבוד שבת, and all the more so not on שבת.

steps.title: Why no fast on Sunday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the people of the מעמד did not fast on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Sunday, what is the reason they did not fast?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explained why there was no fast on Friday and שבת, but it did not say why Sunday was left out. The גמרא asks for that reason, setting up the three answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sunday is not ערב שבת, so the ברייתא's reason does not cover it. The גמרא wants a separate reason for skipping it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the week, Sunday

phrases.english: On Sunday, what is the reason they did not fast?
phrases.notes: Here בשבת means "of the week," so "day one of the week" is Sunday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notices that the ברייתא gave no reason for skipping Sunday.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why didn't the מעמד fast on Sunday?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: because of the Christians
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says they did not fast on Sunday because of the Christians.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: because of the Christians.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer: the reason for not fasting on Sunday has to do with the Christians.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason does not come from the day itself but from the outside world. Sunday was the Christians' special day, and fasting on it could cause problems with them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Because of the Christians.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No fast on Sunday because of the Christians.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: the third day after creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives a different reason: Sunday is the third day after creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: because it is the third day after creation.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another answer to the same question, based on the day's place in the count from creation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי יוחנן, רבי שמואל בר נחמני finds the reason in the day itself. Counting from Friday, when man was created, Sunday is the third day, a weak and delicate day, so it is not a fitting day to fast.

keyTerms.meaning: The third day after creation (of man)

steps.whatToRemember: There is no fast on Friday or שבת because of כבוד שבת. Sunday has two answers: רבי יוחנן says because of the Christians, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני says because it is the third day after creation.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
Because it is the third day after creation.
phrases.notes: He means Sunday is the third day counting from Friday, when man was created.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא שְׁלִישִׁי לַיְצִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than רבי יוחנן to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No fast on Sunday because it is the third day after creation.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: The extra soul has just left
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says they did not fast on Sunday because the נשמה יתירה given for שבת is taken away when שבת ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: It is because of the extra soul. ריש לקיש said that an extra soul is given to a person on ערב שבת, and when שבת ends it is taken from him, as it says 'שבת וינפש.' Once he has rested, 'woe, the soul is lost.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to why the מעמד did not fast on Sunday. ריש לקיש says a person is weaker on Sunday because his extra שבת soul has just left him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's reason was about the Christians, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני's was about creation. ריש לקיש's reason is about the person himself: losing the נשמה יתירה leaves him weak, so fasting on Sunday would be too hard. He reads the word וַיִּנָּפַשׁ as 'וַי נֶפֶשׁ', 'woe, the soul'.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra soul a person receives for שבת
The time right after שבת ends
'And was refreshed,' read here as 'woe, a soul'

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement of ריש לקיש is a well-known source for the idea of the נשמה יתירה on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: Because of the extra soul,
as Reish Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה נִיתְּנָה בּוֹ בָּאָדָם בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: An extra soul is given to a person on Shabbat eve,
and at the end of Shabbat they take it from him,
as it says: "He rested and was refreshed."
Once he has rested, woe, the soul is lost.
phrases.notes: He splits וַיִּנָּפַשׁ into two words, וַי נֶפֶשׁ, which means 'woe, a soul.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question in step 13, next to the answers in steps 14 and 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the מעמד did not fast on Sunday
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the נשמה יתירה is taken away after שבת, which leaves a person weak on Sunday
steps.whatToRemember: There is no fast on Friday or שבת because of כבוד שבת. Sunday has three answers: רבי יוחנן says because of the Christians, רבי שמואל בר נחמני says because it is the third day after creation, and ריש לקיש says because the נשמה יתירה has just left.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: The Sunday reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on Sunday they read בראשית and יהי רקיע.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first day they read 'בראשית' and 'יהי רקיע'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes the line of the משנה about what the מעמד read on Sunday, and this sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day the מעמד read the part of the creation story for that day. On Sunday they read the first day of creation (בראשית) and the start of the second day (יהי רקיע).

keyTerms.meaning: The first section of the Torah, the first day of creation
'Let there be a firmament,' the section about the second day

phrases.english: On the first day,
they read "In the beginning" and "Let there be a firmament."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the fasting question and turns to the משנה's list of daily readings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Sunday the מעמד read בראשית and יהי רקיע

steps.title: ברייתא: Two readers for בראשית, one for the firmament
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that בראשית is read by two people and יהי רקיע by one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'בראשית' is read by two people, and 'יהי רקיע' by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells us how many people read each section. This prepares the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said which sections were read. The ברייתא adds the new detail of how many readers: two for בראשית and one for יהי רקיע.

phrases.english: It was taught: "In the beginning" is read by two,
and "Let there be a firmament" by one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the משנה just quoted
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בראשית has two readers; יהי רקיע has one reader

steps.title: Five verses cannot be split between two readers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how two people can read בראשית. It has only five פסוקים, and each reader must read at least three.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that 'יהי רקיע' is read by one, since it is three פסוקים. But why is 'בראשית' read by two? It is five פסוקים, and it was taught: one who reads from the Torah may not read fewer than three פסוקים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Two readers need at least six פסוקים, but בראשית has only five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that each person called to the Torah reads at least three פסוקים. יהי רקיע has three פסוקים, so one reader works well. Five פסוקים split between two people leaves one of them with only two, which breaks the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (first part is fine, but...)
One who reads from the Torah

phrases.english: It makes sense that "Let there be a firmament" is read by one,
since it is three verses.
But "In the beginning" by two, what is the reason?
It is five verses,
and it was taught: One who reads from the Torah
may not read fewer than three verses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that two people read בראשית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two readers need at least six פסוקים, but בראשית has only five

steps.title: רב: The second reader repeats a verse
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the second reader repeats (דולג) the last פסוק the first reader read.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: He repeats.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The second reader goes back one פסוק and reads it again, so each person reads three פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reader reads פסוקים 1-3. The second reader starts again at פסוק 3 and reads 3-5. That gives each reader three פסוקים without cutting any פסוק in half.

keyTerms.meaning: Repeats (going back over a פסוק already read)

steps.confusionAlert: Here דולג means going back and reading a פסוק again. It does not mean skipping ahead.

phrases.english: Rav said: He repeats.
phrases.notes: The second reader goes back and reads the first reader's last פסוק again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical method that meets the three-פסוק rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Five פסוקים cannot give two readers three each
steps.terutzMaskana: Repeat one פסוק, so each reader reads three

steps.title: שמואל: They split a verse in half
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that they split (פוסק) the middle פסוק into two halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: He splits.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different answer. They cut the middle פסוק in half, so each reader gets two and a half פסוקים, which counts as three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With five פסוקים, the third פסוק is divided. The first reader reads 1-2 and half of 3, and the second reads the rest of 3 and then 4-5. Each reader touches three פסוקים and nothing is read twice.

keyTerms.meaning: Splits a פסוק into two parts

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: He splits.
phrases.notes: The middle פסוק is cut in half, and each reader reads one half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 19, different from רב's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Five פסוקים cannot give two readers three each
steps.terutzMaskana: Split the middle פסוק so each reader reads parts of three

steps.title: Why doesn't רב allow splitting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב did not accept שמואל's simpler idea of splitting a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב, who said 'he repeats,' why didn't he say 'he splits'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב preferred repeating over splitting. This sets up רב's reason in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting seems easy and avoids reading anything twice. So the גמרא wants to know what bothered רב about it.

phrases.english: And Rav, who said he repeats,
what is the reason he did not say he splits?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב דְּאָמַר דּוֹלֵג, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר פּוֹסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about רב's view in light of שמואל's
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב rejects splitting a פסוק

steps.title: רב: We may not split a verse משה did not split
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that any פסוק משה רבינו did not divide, we may not divide either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: Any פסוק that משה did not split, we do not split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב's reason. The division of the פסוקים comes from משה, so we may not cut a פסוק in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב the borders of a פסוק are fixed by משה. Splitting one would change them, so he prefers repeating a whole פסוק even though it means reading it twice.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why רב insists on repeating a whole פסוק rather than cutting one. In the next step the גמרא challenges שמואל from a different source, the story of רבי חנינא קרא.

phrases.english: He holds:
Any verse that Moses did not divide,
we do not divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: כׇּל פְּסוּקָא דְּלָא פַּסְקֵיהּ מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק that משה did not divide may not be divided by us

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: Splitting was allowed only for schoolchildren
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how שמואל can allow splitting, when רבי חנינא קרא was allowed to split פסוקים only for teaching children.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said 'he splits.' But may we split? Didn't רבי חנינא קרא say: I had great trouble with רבי חנינא הגדול, and he allowed me to split only for schoolchildren, since it is done to help them learn?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל. It brings a story showing that splitting a פסוק was only allowed with difficulty, and only for teaching children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא קרא taught Torah to children and asked to break up long פסוקים. רבי חנינא הגדול allowed it only for children, because it helps them learn. That suggests splitting is not allowed in other cases, like reading in public.

keyTerms.meaning: Bible expert, one who taught Torah reading

phrases.english: And Shmuel said he splits,
but may we split?
But didn't Rabbi Chanina the Bible expert say:
I had great trouble
with Rabbi Chanina the Great,
phrases.notes: He means it took a lot of effort to get permission from רבי חנינא הגדול.

phrases.english: and he did not allow me to split
except for schoolchildren,
since it is done so they can learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to שמואל's answer in step 21 and challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a פסוק may be split for the Torah reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Splitting was allowed only for teaching children, which shows it is not allowed in other cases

steps.title: שמואל: Splitting is allowed when there is no other way
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that children were allowed because there was no other way, and here too there is no other way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל: there, what is the reason? Because it is not possible otherwise. Here too, it is not possible otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. The reason splitting was allowed for children is that there was no other choice, and the same is true for reading five פסוקים with two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the story differently. The permission was not special to children; it was given because there was no other way. Two readers cannot get three פסוקים each from five without splitting, so the same reason applies here.
steps.whatToRemember: For two readers of five פסוקים: רב says the second reader repeats a פסוק, because we never split a פסוק משה did not split. שמואל says we split the middle פסוק, because splitting is allowed when there is no other way.

phrases.english: And Shmuel would answer:
There, what is the reason?
Because it is not possible otherwise.
Here too, it is not possible otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the reason for the earlier permission and applies it here
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Splitting was a special allowance only for children
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting is allowed whenever there is no other way, which includes this case

steps.title: Why doesn't שמואל simply repeat a verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל chose splitting a verse rather than רב's method of repeating one.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said the reader splits a verse. Why didn't he say the reader repeats a verse?
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier we saw why רב rejected splitting. Now the גמרא turns the question around and asks why שמואל rejected repeating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating a verse (דולג) seems easy and causes no problem with dividing a פסוק. So the גמרא wants to know what bothered שמואל about it.

keyTerms.meaning: Splits, meaning he divides a verse in the middle
Repeats, meaning the second reader goes back and rereads a verse the first reader already read

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: he splits
What is the reason he did not say: he repeats?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 22. That step asked why רב didn't split. This one asks why שמואל didn't repeat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is שמואל's reason for rejecting רב's method of repeating a verse?

steps.title: Repeating could confuse people coming in or going out
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rejects repeating because of a rabbinic decree. People who enter or leave in the middle could misunderstand what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree because of people who come in, and a decree because of people who go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חכמים worried about people who walk into or out of the shul during the reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who only hears part of the reading won't know that a verse was repeated. He may think one reader read fewer than three new verses, and wrongly learn that this is allowed. Splitting a verse doesn't cause this mistake, so שמואל prefers it.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
Those who come in (to the shul in the middle of the reading)
Those who go out (in the middle of the reading)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: we don't split a verse that משה didn't split. שמואל: we don't repeat a verse, because people coming and going could get confused.

phrases.english: A decree because of those who come in
phrases.notes: Someone walking in late doesn't know the verse was a repeat, and may think the first reader read too few verses.

phrases.english: and a decree because of those who go out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Repeating a verse could mislead people who enter or leave mid-reading into thinking fewer than three verses per reader is allowed, so the חכמים decreed against it.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a five-verse paragraph
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a five-verse paragraph is read by one person. If two read it, the second continues into the next paragraph.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: A paragraph of six verses is read by two people, and one of five verses by one person. If the first reads three, the second reads two from this paragraph and one from the next paragraph. Some say he reads three from the next one, because we don't start a paragraph with fewer than three verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to challenge both רב and שמואל. This step sets up the source, and the next step spells out the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reader needs at least three verses. Six verses divide neatly between two people, but five do not. In that case the ברייתא doesn't say to repeat or to split. It sends the second reader on into the next paragraph.

keyTerms.meaning: A paragraph or section of the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions in the ברייתא agree that the second reader moves into the next paragraph. They only argue about how many verses he reads there: one or three.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A paragraph of six verses
is read by two people
and one of five, by one person.
And if the first reads three
the second reads two from this paragraph
and one from another paragraph.
And some say: three
phrases.notes: He reads three verses from the next paragraph, not just one.

phrases.english: because one does not begin a paragraph
with fewer than three verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both methods have been explained, the גמרא brings a source that seems to use neither method.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a similar case of a five-verse paragraph, the ברייתא solves the problem by moving to the next paragraph rather than repeating or splitting.

steps.title: Why doesn't the ברייתא repeat or split?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge. According to רב the second reader should repeat a verse, and according to שמואל he should split one.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says repeat, let him repeat. According to the one who says split, let him split!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the challenge from the ברייתא clear: each אמורא's own method should have been used there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If repeating or splitting is the right way to handle a short paragraph, the ברייתא should have said so. It went to another paragraph instead, so it seems to disagree with both רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: According to the one who says repeat, let him repeat
and according to the one who says split, let him split!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דּוֹלֵג לִידְלוֹג וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר פּוֹסֵק לִיפְסוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains exactly how the ברייתא of step 28 is a problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא skips both methods, which suggests that neither repeating nor splitting is the proper solution.

steps.title: The case there is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: the case in the ברייתא is different from ours.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there.
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening of the answer. The גמרא is setting up the next move, and the explanation of what is different comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שאני התם' tells us the גמרא will not reject רב or שמואל. Instead it will show that the ברייתא's case has a special feature that allows moving on to another paragraph.

phrases.english: It is different there,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to answer the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's case seemed the same as the case of רב and שמואל, so it seemed to reject both.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's case has a special feature (explained next) that makes moving to another paragraph possible there.
